cards.text: Chronicles opened with Adam and walked us down through the nations (1 Chronicles 1). Now it reaches the twelve sons of Israel, the name God gave Jacob (Genesis 32:28): Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Joseph, Benjamin and six more. TWELVE boys, friend, and I needed a nap after raising six cookie cutters.
Judah's first three sons are born to him by Bath-shua the Canaanite: Er, Onan and Shelah. Er is the firstborn, and the list stops right here to say the LORD put him to death.

cards.question: Er, Judah's firstborn, was ___ in the sight of the LORD.

cards.text: Then Tamar, Judah's daughter-in-law, bears him two more sons, Perez and Zerah. Perez has two sons, Hezron and Hamul, and Zerah has five.

cards.question: Next in the list is Carmi's son Achar, and his name comes with a note attached. Achar brought ___ upon Israel by violating the ban on devoted things.

cards.text: Hezron has three sons: Jerahmeel, Ram and Caleb (not Caleb son of Jephunneh, who scouted Canaan). Ram's line runs down through Nahshon, a leader of Judah's descendants, then Boaz from the book of Ruth (Ruth 4:21), then Obed and Jesse. Jesse's sons are listed oldest first, and the seventh and last is David, the shepherd boy who becomes king (1 Samuel 16:11-13; 2 Samuel 5:3). The youngest one, at the very end of the line? Friend, I spent years at the very back of a junk drawer, so this one makes me want to stand up and CHEER.
David's sister Zeruiah has three sons, Abishai, Joab and Asahel, and Joab grows up to command David's army (2 Samuel 8:16).

Caleb son of Hezron has sons by Azubah, and when Azubah dies he marries Ephrath, who bears him Hur. Hur's grandson is Bezalel, the craftsman God filled with skill to make the Tent of Meeting (Exodus 31:2-7).

Later, Hezron has a son, Segub, by the daughter of Machir the father of Gilead, and Segub's son Jair has twenty-three cities in the land of Gilead. Twenty-three cities? I've got ONE planet, and it's just big enough for a bakery.

cards.question: Right after Jair's cities in the land of Gilead, the list says "But…" What happens to Havvoth-jair, and to Kenath with its villages?

cards.text: After Hezron dies in Caleb-ephrathah, his wife Abijah bears him Ashhur the father of Tekoa. Then come the descendants of Jerahmeel, Hezron's firstborn, through two wives, and twice the list notes a man who died without children.
One of Jerahmeel's descendants, Sheshan, has no sons, only daughters. He also has an Egyptian servant named Jarha.

cards.question: Sheshan has daughters but no sons, and an Egyptian servant named Jarha. What does Sheshan do?

answers.text: Gives Jarha a daughter in marriage

cards.text: Sheshan's daughter bears Jarha a son, Attai, and from there the line runs father to son for generations, all the way down to Elishama.

Then the list comes back to Caleb, Jerahmeel's brother: his sons, the sons of his concubines, and his daughter Acsah. Along the way are men called the father of Ziph, the father of Beth-zur, even Salma the father of Bethlehem. It closes with clans, like the clans of the scribes who lived at Jabez. That's a LOT of names, friend, and I've stamped fewer cookies on a holiday weekend.

Now the list reaches David's own sons. Six are born to him in Hebron, each by a different mother: Amnon first, then Daniel (not the prophet Daniel), then Absalom and three more. David reigns in Hebron seven years and six months, and then in Jerusalem thirty-three years.

In Jerusalem, Bathsheba daughter of Ammiel bears him four sons, including Nathan (not Nathan the prophet) and Solomon. Then come nine more sons, and two of them are named Eliphelet, so I bet calling those boys in from outside got confusing real quick. There are also sons by his concubines, and the boys have a sister named Tamar (not the Tamar who was Judah's daughter-in-law).

Then the list follows Solomon's line, father to son: Rehoboam, Abijah, Asa, Jehoshaphat, and on down through Hezekiah, Manasseh, Amon and Josiah. Josiah has four sons, and after Jehoiakim come his son Jeconiah, and Zedekiah. Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim is carried away to Babylon (Jeremiah 24:1).

cards.question: Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, carried away to Babylon (Jeremiah 24:1), gets one word next to his name in this list. He's Jeconiah the ___.
In this list, David's line ends with Jeconiah.

cards.text: Jeconiah's line keeps going: his sons Shealtiel and Pedaiah, then Pedaiah's son Zerubbabel, and on down through Hananiah, Shecaniah and Neariah to Elioenai's seven sons. This family tree is like the group chat you muted three days ago: you peek back in and it's at FOUR HUNDRED messages.
